To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FANCD2, a protein mutated in Fanconi anemia, is a target for ubiquitination and colocalizes with BRCA1 in nuclear foci.
the Fanconi anema (FA) protein complex interacts with the breast cancer 1 (BRCA1) protein and that the FA proteins and BRCA 1 function together in the same cellular pathway.

the Fanconi anemias are a group of genetic disorders that cause sensitivity to DNA cross-linking agents and ionizing radiation and that the FANCD1/BRCA2 gene is the first gene to be identified as the cause of the Fanconi syndrome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the cellular processes that lead to cancer and other genetic diseases.
the identification of the Fanconi Anemia pathway, a cellular pathway that repairs interstrand crosslinks and is disrupted in patients with Fanconi Anemia.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the Fanconi anemaia (FA) pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the FA pathway is a DNA repair pathway that involves the monoubiquitination of FANCD2 in response to DNA crosslinks and that this monoubiquitinylation is essential for the cellular function of the FANCA/FANCC/FANCG complex.

the Fanconi anemias are a family of autosomal recessive disorders that are characterized by cellular hypersensitivity to DNA-damaging agents, and are associated with chromosomal breakage, developmental anomalies, bone marrow failure, and an increased predisposition to malignancies.
FA is a DNA repair disorder, and the FANCD protein is a critical component of this repair pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FA protein complex is required for the monoubiquitination of FANCD2, which in turn is required for the recruitment of BRCA1 into nuclear foci in response to DNA double strand breaks.
FANCA, CC, C, and G proteins are part of a complex that is required for the monoubiquitination of FANCD2 and that the FANCD protein is required to activate BRCA1 in response to DNA damaging agents.
the FA proteins form a complex with BRCA1 and that the FA pathway functions in the repair of DNA interstrand cross-links.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FA proteins, FANCA, -B, -C, -E, -F, and -G, and the breast cancer susceptibility gene, BRCA1, function in a common DNA repair pathway.
the FA pathway is an integral part of the DNA repair process and is required for the maintenance of genomic stability.
the Fanconi anema proteins and BRCA 1 are part of the same pathway.
